selection_rationale: Figure 2b reports experimental frequency sweeps from the same fluorinated sample at four complete XY8 block counts. It is the closest located published experimental approximation to a timing-depth surface.

source.citation: S. J. DeVience et al., Nanoscale NMR spectroscopy and imaging of multiple nuclear species, Nature Nanotechnology 10, 129-134 (2015).
source.sample: fluorinated PFOS/POSF sample measured with a single shallow NV centre

vertical_offset_correction.source: caption states that spectra are offset vertically; dashed baselines occur at 1.6, 1.4, 1.2, and 1.0

normalization_policy.measured_surface: divide all four measured rows by one global measured-response maximum
normalization_policy.predicted_surface: if evaluated, normalize independently by its own global optimum
normalization_policy.purpose: preserve the published depth dependence while preventing any absolute-scale comparison

topology_policy.rectangularization: linear interpolation of each measured row onto the frozen common grid without extrapolation
topology_policy.connectivity: four-neighbour on the sampled frequency-depth grid
topology_policy.negative_response_treatment: clip response values below zero to zero as physically non-resonant baseline fluctuations
topology_policy.high_threshold_guardrail: thresholds above 60% admit baseline noise and are exported but not interpreted as stable resonant topology

digitization_policy.method: extract marker-object centers from the vector PDF in the arXiv source archive
digitization_policy.error_scope: digitization only; the publication does not show pointwise experimental error bars in Figure 2b

interpretation_guardrail: This surface tests whether connected resonance structure transfers across four XY8 depths. It does not validate the project's 200 kHz sensitivity optimum or establish that N=20 is optimal for the DeVience device.
